MD-2026-SB448.aiSummary: The bill would let Carroll County borrow up to $27 million for public facilities, including water and sewer projects, roads, bridges, schools, county buildings, and parks. It would also let the county make loans to volunteer fire departments for equipment, buildings, and other related needs, and use some borrowing to buy farm or woodland easements. The county would have to repay the bonds with property taxes, and the bond income would be exempt from Maryland taxes.

MD-2026-SB791.aiSummary: The law limits how state and local correctional facilities and law enforcement can work with federal immigration authorities. It bars many checks, holds, transfers, and threats based on a person’s immigration status, with some exceptions, and it requires state facilities to give notice before release in some cases with an active immigration detainer. It also lets the attorney general or an affected person sue to enforce the rules and seek damages or a court order.

MD-2026-SB322.aiSummary: The law changes when a person with a criminal conviction can be kept off a jury in Maryland. It says a person is not qualified if they are still serving a sentence, including parole or probation, for certain crimes, or if they were convicted of perjury, witness intimidation, jury intimidation, or a crime under Title 8 of the Criminal Law Article. It also keeps people with pending charges for a crime punishable by more than 1 year in prison from serving, and it takes effect October 1, 2026.

MD-2026-HB1335.aiSummary: The law requires the Department of Information Technology to hire a third party to study state staffing and skills needs for information technology and cybersecurity jobs. The study must look at current positions, gaps in needed skills, pay comparisons, and ways to improve hiring and retention for state tech workers. The department must send the study to the Governor and the General Assembly by November 1, 2027; the law takes effect July 1, 2026, and ends June 30, 2028.

MD-2026-SB805.aiSummary: The bill changes Maryland’s student loan debt tax credit. It would let the Maryland Higher Education Commission extend the time for some people to use the credit to pay student loans, and it would make people repay only the unused part of the credit if they do not use all of it in time. The credit is for qualified taxpayers with at least $20,000 in student loan debt and at least $5,000 still owed, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026, for tax years after December 31, 2025.

MD-2026-SB532.aiSummary: Public senior colleges and community colleges in Maryland would have to report each year on how students can get over-the-counter birth control on campus. Community colleges would also have to give students access to all types of over-the-counter contraception, such as through a health center, campus stores, vending machines, or another way that works on campus. The reports would go to the Maryland Higher Education Commission, which would send a yearly report to lawmakers. The law takes effect July 1, 2026.

It also makes the exemption apply back to tax years starting after June 30, 2023, and requires refunds for excess tax paid because of that change. The act takes effect June 1, 2026.

It also creates sports activity venue licenses for places like bowling centers, golf simulators, pickleball courts, gyms, and similar sites, with rules for where alcohol can be sold, food service, staff training, and crowd control. MD-2026-HB121.aiSummary: In Baltimore County, this law lets certain restaurants and bars with Class B or Class D licenses apply to sell mixed drinks and cocktails for takeout if the county licensing board adopts rules first. The drink must be bought with prepared food, the buyer must be 21 or older with valid ID, and the drink must be in a sealed container and sold by 11 p.m. The board may not charge an extra fee for this, may set a limit on how much one person can buy in one sale, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
